Okay, let’s gauge individual investor and public sentiment independently.

Should Jensen Huang remain CEO of $NVDA?

Regarding $NBIS earnings results:

To show you how fast they're growing... from Q2 to Q3: 

Revenue: $582.3M -> $980.8M (+68% QoQ)
Adjusted EBITDA: $236.2M -> $465.8M (+97% QoQ)
AI cloud adj. EBITDA margin: 49.7% -> 53.2%
Net Income: −$190.4M -> −$37.5M

ARR has reached $6.4B at the end of Sep. In terms of management commentary: 

- Since start of Q3, Nebius signed $12B+ of new contracts
- Average GPU pricing rose 20%+ sequentially, payback shortened from 22M -> 19M
- On Q3 deals, prepayments covered 100% of associated capex, up from 50–60% in Q2 (insane for financing)
- Contract value per MW exceeded $25M+ from Q3 up from ~$20M Q2 
- 5GW contracted power year end

With $10B of committed customer prepayments in 2026 and $17B-$20B in 2027. Now, prepayments and borrowing against existing contracts covers ~75-85% of 2027 capex. 

On subsidiaries:
1. Avride - 250 autonomous vehicles fleet, over 100,000 passenger rides (with companies like $UBER). Fully driverless robotaxi targeted H1 2027.
2. Toloka - Revenue doubled sequentially
3. Enterprise cloud - Databricks and Datadog selected Neibus. Along with a new agreement with Snowflake. 
4. Tavily - Over 3M developers now with $IBM post-training a core partner. 
5. ClickHouse - Nothing about new secondary valuations, but we can see valuations growing
6. TokenFactory - Contract value grew 17x sequentially

The primary negative I saw was that 2026 guidance is now on the lower end (near ~$3B), due to $MSFT capacity deliveries slipping to Q2 2027.

Apparently there was an execution miss with a third party partner DataOne. Temporary generators were retired amid permitting issues before enough $BE fuel cell capacity came online. 

Capex also increased in 2026 from $20B-$25B to $27B, while revising revenue expectations downward. 

So near-term unfortunate headwinds kinda reminiscent of AOI earnings; however long term I think Nebius will take care of you. 

For 2027 outlook:
- $12-13 billion revenue, capex of $40-45 billion, pre-tax breakeven by the end of 2027.

Very operationally bullish, as seen with prepayments covering capex, GPU premiums increasing. Main downside is near-term execution risk from third parties, causing near-term delays and revenue recognition. 

Great quarter from Nebius overall.
@aleabitoreddit Why did it tank on these good news

So there's the positive fundamental long term outlook that I've interpreted. 

On the other hand, there's near term headwinds that I highlighted above, which markets are pricing in. 

Negatives I saw near term were $MSFT Vineland pushing back into Q2 2027, which delays revenue recognition. 

Alongside 2026/2027 capex hikes + downward revision of next quarter revenue. We've seen markets punish near term execution delays with $AAOI recently too. 

For long term, I don't see this earnings as negative, given 100% prepayments, compute prices going up, new contracts and their subsidiaries growing.

text:
AI is expanding what game developers can afford to attempt.

The opportunities fall along two dimensions: whether AI is helping with an existing game or a new one, and whether its main contribution is lower cost or new possibilities.

Indie devs can now do more with lean teams, toolmakers can decompile and modify existing games, and studios can take riskier bets on original IP and experimental genres.

Some of gaming's biggest franchises began with someone tinkering with an existing game. AI gives more people a place to start.

Full piece from a16z's Elena Burger, Anish Acharya, and Jon Lai: http://a16z.news/p/gamings-next-origin-stories

a16z's Jon Lai on why AI could shorten game development cycles and enable game studios to take riskier bets:

"One of the structural challenges in games is that it just takes a really long time to make these games, right? Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in production since 2013, 2014. It's a 12, 13-year development cycle."

"By any other software development standard, right? Taking 10-plus years to make HR software or CRM, it's kind of insane, right?"

"Let's see if we can get a 5 to 10-year dev cycle to, I don't know, 2 to 5 years. It's still going to take some time, but I think it'll just enable game developers to take more risk, have more at-bats, take more experiments, and just generally increase the richness and diversity of games that are created."

AI can help defend America's critical infrastructure as fast as attackers now operate.

Much of the equipment running power grids, water systems, and other essential services is decades old. Some of it can't be patched without risking an outage.

a16z's Anne Neuberger proposes a public-private defense plan focused on the few hundred operators and shared vendors whose failure could cascade nationally, across power, banking and payments, water, communications, and hospitals.

Super Intelligence-Era Critical Infrastructure Cyber Defense Plan: http://a16z.news/p/super-intelligence-era-critical-infrastructure

quoted_tweet.author: Anne Neuberger
quoted_tweet.text:
We cannot defend America’s infrastructure at human speed against attacks moving at machine speed.

In today’s WSJ, I make the case for using AI to protect the systems that keep our water flowing, hospitals operating and lights on.

Here’s the action plan: https://www.a16z.news/p/super-intelligence-era-critical-infrastructure

- Start with the few hundred operators and shared suppliers whose failure could cascade nationally.
-The White House must set outcome-based goals, like ensuring control systems aren't exposed to the Internet.
- Use AI to find and fix flaws. Contain what cannot be patched. Test whether essential services can keep running under attack.
- CEOs of critical infrastructure firms should be accountable for these outcome-based results.
- The White House, infrastructure operators, AI labs and technology providers each have a role. AI labs, for example, should work with critical infrastructure operators to build digital replicas so high risk patches can be tested offline.

AI can give defenders an advantage. We need to organize to use it.
https://www.wsj.com/opinion/cyberattacks-are-coming-for-us-all-b19b46d4
